settings.title: Terms that govern customer accounts and private delivery.
settings.body: These terms explain access, billing, customer usage, and the responsibilities of the site owner and customer.

settings.title: Terms of service
settings.body:
1. Acceptance

By using this site, you agree to these terms and to the privacy policy that governs uploads, generated outputs, purchases, and private delivery.

2. Accounts

Customers must provide accurate account information and keep credentials secure. Each account belongs to the photo workspace and cannot be shared across unrelated site customer records.

3. Subscriptions and credits

Subscriptions and one-time credit packs provide credits for AI photo generation. Credits are granted after confirmed payment, reserved when a job starts, consumed after successful delivery, and released when a job fails or times out.

4. Refunds

Unused credits may be reviewed for refund eligibility within 30 days. Credits already spent on successful generations are not refundable unless support confirms a service-side technical failure.

5. Uploaded content

You may only upload images and references you control or have permission to use. The site may reject, review, remove, or block content that violates law, platform rules, or safety policy.

6. Delivery

Completed jobs are delivered to the signed-in customer account. Delivery states, retries, credit releases, and refunds are handled by the backend and recorded in your credit history.

7. Liability

The service is provided as a software subscription. To the extent permitted by law, liability is limited to the fees paid for the current billing period or the affected credit purchase.

8. Contact us

Email support@mydreamshoots.com for account, billing, refund, or policy questions.

settings.title: How cookies support sign-in, checkout, and private albums.
settings.body: This policy explains the cookies and local storage used on www.mydreamshoots.com for the MyDreamShoots AI photo service.

settings.title: Cookie policy
settings.body:
1. What cookies are

Cookies are small files stored by your browser. MyDreamShoots also uses similar browser storage, such as local storage, to keep the AI photo service secure, usable, and consistent while you move between packages, checkout, your account, and private albums.

2. Essential cookies

Essential cookies support customer sign-in, scoped sessions, CSRF protection, checkout continuity, credit reservation flows, private album access, rate limiting, fraud prevention, and secure admin or customer authentication. These cookies are required for the core service and cannot be switched off inside the site without breaking key features.

3. Preference storage

We may remember practical preferences such as menu state, recently opened workspace views, selected package context, language or display choices if available, and browser-side UI settings. This helps MyDreamShoots open the right customer workspace more quickly.

4. Performance and diagnostics

We may collect limited technical signals to understand slow pages, failed requests, broken checkout steps, job submission errors, and account access issues. These signals help us improve route speed, generation reliability, and customer support.

5. Analytics and measurement

If analytics tools are enabled, they may help us understand aggregated usage such as popular package categories, tool discovery, pricing page visits, and conversion paths. Analytics should not be used to sell your uploaded photos or generated images.

6. Payment, email, hosting, and AI providers

Connected providers may set or read cookies or similar identifiers when needed for checkout, anti-fraud checks, email delivery, hosting security, media storage, or AI generation. Their use is limited to providing and protecting the requested service.

7. Your browser controls

You can block, delete, or limit cookies in your browser settings. If you block essential cookies, MyDreamShoots may not be able to keep you signed in, complete checkout, reserve credits, start generation jobs, or open private albums.

8. Relationship to privacy policy

Cookie data is handled together with the privacy practices described in our Privacy Policy. The Terms of Service explain customer responsibilities when using accounts, credits, uploads, and generated outputs.

9. Updates and contact

We may update this Cookie Policy as we add or remove providers, analytics, checkout methods, or security features. Email support@mydreamshoots.com with cookie or tracking questions.

settings.title: Terms that govern customer accounts and private delivery.
settings.body: These terms explain access, billing, customer usage, and the responsibilities of the site owner and customer.

settings.title: Terms of service
settings.body:
1. Acceptance

By using this site, you agree to these terms and to the privacy policy that governs uploads, generated outputs, purchases, and private delivery.

2. Accounts

Customers must provide accurate account information and keep credentials secure. Each account belongs to the photo workspace and cannot be shared across unrelated site customer records.

3. Subscriptions and credits

Subscriptions and one-time credit packs provide credits for AI photo generation. Credits are granted after confirmed payment, reserved when a job starts, consumed after successful delivery, and released when a job fails or times out.

4. Refunds

Unused credits may be reviewed for refund eligibility within 30 days. Credits already spent on successful generations are not refundable unless support confirms a service-side technical failure.

5. Uploaded content

You may only upload images and references you control or have permission to use. The site may reject, review, remove, or block content that violates law, platform rules, or safety policy.

6. Delivery

Completed jobs are delivered to the signed-in customer account. Delivery states, retries, credit releases, and refunds are handled by the backend and recorded in your credit history.

7. Liability

The service is provided as a software subscription. To the extent permitted by law, liability is limited to the fees paid for the current billing period or the affected credit purchase.

8. Contact us

Email support@mydreamshoots.com for account, billing, refund, or policy questions.

You may only upload images and references you control or have permission to use. The site may reject, review, remove, or block content that violates law, platform rules, or safety policy.

6. Delivery

Completed jobs are delivered to the signed-in customer account. Delivery states, retries, credit releases, and refunds are handled by the backend and recorded in your credit history.

7. Liability

The service is provided as a software subscription. To the extent permitted by law, liability is limited to the fees paid for the current billing period or the affected credit purchase.

Email support@mydreamshoots.com for account, billing, refund, or policy questions.

settings.question: What is the refund policy?

settings.question: When are credits used?
settings.answer: Credit cost is shown before each generation. Different packages may use different credit amounts based on style, output size, and generation settings.

settings.question: Why do premium packs need a private model?
settings.answer: A private model keeps the customer's face and style consistent across different photo packages. Studio tools can help prepare inputs, while premium albums use the model for better continuity.

settings.question: What happens if I cancel a plan?
settings.answer: Access to previous albums follows the account and gallery policy. New package requests may require an active plan or enough available credits.

settings.question: Can I try MyDreamShoots for free?
settings.answer: Some lightweight tools can be free. Private model creation and premium photo packages require credits because they use dedicated generation capacity.

settings.question: What photos should I upload?
settings.answer: Recent, clear, high-quality phone photos work best. Use different angles, expressions, lighting, and outfits so the private model has enough visual range.

settings.question: Are my uploaded photos private?
settings.answer: Yes. Source photos, generation jobs, albums, orders, and credits stay connected to your signed-in MyDreamShoots account and are not public by default.

settings.question: What is the refund policy?
settings.answer: Refund eligibility follows the site policy and checkout terms. Credits already spent on successful generations are not refundable, while failed requests can return reserved credits according to request status.

settings.question: When are credits used?
settings.answer: Credit cost is shown before each generation. Different packages may use different credit amounts based on style, output size, and generation settings.

settings.question: Why do premium packs need a private model?
settings.answer: A private model keeps the customer's face and style consistent across different photo packages. Studio tools can help prepare inputs, while premium albums use the model for better continuity.

settings.question: What happens if I cancel a plan?
settings.answer: Access to previous albums follows the account and gallery policy. New package requests may require an active plan or enough available credits.

settings.title: Privacy policy
settings.body:
1. Information we collect

We collect the email address used for your account, source photos you upload, generation settings, payment status, credit movements, and delivered outputs needed to operate the service.

2. How we use data

We use your data to create AI photo packages, manage credits and subscriptions, deliver private galleries, provide support, prevent abuse, and improve product reliability.

3. Photo privacy

Uploads and generated images stay tied to the current site and customer account. We do not sell personal photos, and site data is kept separate from other storefronts.

4. Payments

Payments are processed by Stripe or the connected payment account for this storefront. We store billing state and ledger records, not full card numbers.

5. Security

The service is served over HTTPS. Access to private albums, customer assets, jobs, and billing records is scoped by site and customer session.

6. Retention and deletion

You may request deletion of uploaded assets or generated outputs. Some billing, ledger, and abuse-prevention records may be retained where legally or operationally required.

7. Contact

Email support@mydreamshoots.com for privacy, account, or deletion requests.

settings.title: Refund policy
settings.body:
Refund eligibility

You may request a refund for purchased credits if none of the credits from that purchase have been used. Once credits have been spent on a successful generation, that purchase becomes non-refundable.

Refund window

Refund requests should be submitted within 30 days of the purchase date with your account email and purchase details.

Subscriptions

If a subscription is canceled, the customer keeps access to purchased credits until they are used or expire according to the plan rules. Cancellation does not automatically refund credits already used.

Technical failures

If a technical failure on our side prevents credit use or delivery, support may release credits, rerun the job, or approve a refund after review.

Credit history

Refunds and billing reversals appear in the customer's credit history. Checkout completion never grants credits before payment confirmation, and every adjustment is recorded for account support.

settings.title: Shipping and Digital Delivery Policy
settings.body:
No physical shipping

MyDreamShoots sells digital AI photo credits, generated image packages, downloads, and private gallery access. We do not ship physical products, printed photos, USB drives, or mailed merchandise from this storefront.

Digital delivery

Credits are added after payment confirmation. Generated images are delivered inside the signed-in customer workspace or private gallery when a job completes. Delivery timing can vary based on source photo quality, selected package settings, provider availability, moderation review, and system load.

Failed or delayed jobs

If a service-side issue prevents delivery, support may release reserved credits, rerun the job, troubleshoot the account, or review refund eligibility under the refund policy.

No carrier tracking or customs

Because orders are digital, customers do not receive carrier tracking numbers and are not charged shipping, customs, duties, or physical handling fees by MyDreamShoots.

Contact

Email support@mydreamshoots.com with the account email, order or job details, and a short description if a digital delivery does not appear in the workspace.

settings.title: Terms of Service
settings.body:
1. Acceptance

By using this site, you agree to these terms and to the privacy policy that governs uploads, generated outputs, purchases, and private delivery.

2. Accounts

Customers must provide accurate account information and keep credentials secure. Each account belongs to the current storefront and cannot be shared across unrelated site customer records.

3. Subscriptions and credits

Subscriptions and one-time credit packs provide credits for AI photo generation. Credits are granted after confirmed payment, reserved when a job starts, consumed after successful delivery, and released when a job fails or times out.

4. Refunds

Unused credits may be reviewed for refund eligibility within 30 days. Credits already spent on successful generations are not refundable unless support confirms a service-side technical failure.

5. Uploaded content

You may only upload images and references you control or have permission to use. The site may reject, review, remove, or block content that violates law, platform rules, or safety policy.

6. Delivery

Completed jobs are delivered to the signed-in customer account. Delivery states, retries, credit releases, and refunds are handled by the backend and recorded in the ledger.

7. Liability

The service is provided as a software subscription. To the extent permitted by law, liability is limited to the fees paid for the current billing period or the affected credit purchase.

8. Contact us

Email support@mydreamshoots.com for account, billing, refund, or policy questions.

settings.title: How to prepare source photos for cleaner AI photo packages
settings.summary: A practical guide to choosing the selfies, angles, lighting, wardrobe variety, and permission checks that help MyDreamShoots produce cleaner private photo sets.
settings.author: MyDreamShoots editorial team
settings.imageAlt: Private source photo upload workspace for MyDreamShoots
settings.body:
Better AI photo results usually start with calmer inputs. MyDreamShoots can follow a package direction more reliably when the source photos show the person clearly, from a few natural angles, without filters that hide face shape, hairline, skin tone, or expression.

What the generator needs from you

Use source photos that show the same person in simple lighting. A good set includes one close portrait, one half-body frame, one relaxed expression, and one different angle. The goal is not a perfect studio shoot. The goal is enough consistent information for the private request to understand identity before it builds a new scene.

Choose clear inputs before stylish ones

Start with sharp, recent images where the face is visible and the background is not competing for attention. Avoid heavy beauty filters, extreme crops, sunglasses, busy group photos, and pictures where the face is partly covered. A stylish photo can be useful later, but a clear photo should lead the set.

Add range without confusing the brief

Variation helps when it stays organized. Include different expressions, lighting, and camera distances, but avoid mixing many hairstyles, costume changes, or old photos from different life stages in the same request. If you want a new hairstyle, fantasy scene, fan poster, or business headshot, let the package brief carry the change instead of forcing every source image to show a different version of you.

Match photos to the package outcome

Professional headshot packages benefit from clean face detail and neutral clothing. Creator portraits can use more personality, gestures, and outfit notes. Fan posters and cinematic worlds can handle stronger mood references, but still need a stable identity base. When in doubt, choose the photos that make the person easiest to recognize.

Keep privacy and permissions simple

Only upload photos you own or have permission to use. If the package involves another person, make sure they expect their image to be used in a private AI photo workflow. Finished results stay tied to the signed-in MyDreamShoots account, where you can review, download, and decide what belongs outside the private gallery.

Source-photo checklist

CheckWhy it matters
Recent, sharp portraitsHelps the result preserve identity and current details.
Natural expressionsGives packages more usable options for professional, social, or cinematic scenes.
Simple lightingReduces shadows and color shifts before generation begins.
Permission-safe uploadsKeeps private albums and account records easier to manage.

Mistakes that lower result quality

The weakest source sets usually have the same pattern: one very polished selfie, one filtered social post, and several photos where the face is small or turned away. That combination asks the system to guess too much. It may still produce attractive images, but the person can drift between outputs because the identity evidence is uneven.

Another common issue is mixing different life stages in one upload. A current photo, an old vacation photo, and a heavily edited formal image can all be meaningful to the customer, but they are not equally useful for generation. If your goal is a photo package that looks like you now, make the current images the base set.

How many photos should you upload?

More photos are not automatically better. A smaller group of clear, consistent portraits usually beats a large folder of mixed screenshots. For a first MyDreamShoots set, think in terms of coverage: front-facing, slight side angle, different expression, and one frame that shows hair and shoulders clearly. If a photo repeats the same angle and lighting as another, keep the sharper one.

Source photo FAQ

Can I use phone selfies?

Yes. Phone selfies can work well when they are sharp, recent, and naturally lit. The main thing to avoid is a selfie that has been softened by filters or compressed through multiple apps before upload.

Should I upload professional photos?

Professional portraits can help if they still look like the person and do not rely on extreme retouching. A clean studio photo is useful for headshots, while relaxed everyday photos often help lifestyle and creator packages feel more natural.

What if I want a different hairstyle or outfit?

Use source photos for identity and use the package choice or style notes for transformation. If every source photo shows a different hairstyle, the request has less stable information to follow.

Once the source set is ready, compare the package direction and visible credit cost before generation. That small pause is often what turns a random upload into a cleaner finished gallery.

settings.title: How to choose the right AI photo package before spending credits
settings.summary: Use the final use case, source-photo needs, style risk, output count, and visible credit cost to decide which MyDreamShoots package belongs in your next private set.
settings.author: MyDreamShoots editorial team
settings.imageAlt: MyDreamShoots package wall with AI portrait styles
settings.body:
Choosing a package is easier when you start with the job the images need to do. A headshot, a creator profile, a fan poster, and a cinematic portrait can all use the same account credits, but they ask different things from your source photos and your review process.

Start with the final use

Pick the package that matches where the finished images will live. LinkedIn-style portraits need clarity and restraint. Social profile sets can use stronger expression and crop variety. Holiday cards, fan posters, and cinematic scenes can carry more atmosphere because the final image is meant to feel themed.

Compare source-photo needs

If you only have a few clean selfies, start with a package that does not depend on complex poses or dramatic costumes. If you have several clear angles, you can choose a more expressive package because the workflow has more identity context to work from.

Check the credit cost before generation

MyDreamShoots shows the credit cost before a private job starts. Use that moment to decide whether you want a focused set now or a broader gallery later. If you are testing a new look, a smaller package can help you learn what works before spending more credits on a larger album.

Decide how much style risk you want

Cleaner professional packages usually carry less visual risk because the scene is restrained. Fantasy, sports, event, and cinematic packages can be more dramatic, which also means you should review outputs carefully before using them publicly. Choose the package that matches your comfort with transformation.

Decide where the photos will be used

A package feels easier to judge when you name the destination for the finished images. A resume portrait needs a calmer crop and a face-forward expression. A creator profile can accept more gesture, color, and crop variety. A fan poster or holiday scene can be judged by mood, but it still needs enough identity consistency that friends recognize the person without reading the caption.

Write the intended use in plain language before choosing the package. "Three profile options for LinkedIn" leads to a different choice than "a private album of cinematic portraits for a birthday surprise." That short sentence helps you avoid buying a style because it looks exciting while missing the use case that actually matters.

Quick comparison

Package goalBest source-photo matchReview focus
Professional headshotsClear face detail, neutral clothing, low visual clutter.Identity, crop, expression, and background restraint.
Creator portraitsSeveral expressions, some outfit variety, natural body posture.Personality, usable crops, and social profile fit.
Themed albumsStable identity photos plus one clear mood direction.Scene consistency, costume fit, and artifact checks.
Small test setYour sharpest two or three current portraits.Whether the direction is worth a larger credit spend.

Use related guides as planning tools

Before starting, read source-photo guidance and private gallery notes. Then open packages and compare the package description, credit cost, and intended output. That creates a simple decision path: purpose first, source-photo fit second, credits third.

A simple package-choice framework

  • Need one polished identity look? Choose headshots or profile portraits.
  • Need expressive social content? Choose creator, lifestyle, beauty, or themed album sets.
  • Need a specific event mood? Choose holiday, sports, wedding, fan, or cinematic packages.
  • Need to test first? Start smaller, review privately, then spend more credits when the direction is clear.

Package planning FAQ

Should I start with the smallest package?

Start small when you are testing a new look, a new source-photo set, or a dramatic style. Choose a larger package when the intended use is clear and you already know the source photos represent you well.

How do I avoid wasting credits?

Check three things before generation: whether the package matches the final use, whether the source photos are clear enough, and whether the visible credit cost feels right for the number of images you expect to review.

Can one package cover every style?

Usually no. A focused package creates a cleaner gallery. If you want professional headshots and cinematic posters, treat them as separate requests so each set has a clear visual job.

The best package is not always the biggest one. It is the one that fits your source photos, your intended use, and the amount of review you want before downloading favorites.

A package feels easier to judge when you name the destination for the finished images. A resume portrait needs a calmer crop and a face-forward expression. A creator profile can accept more gesture, color, and crop variety. A fan poster or holiday scene can be judged by mood, but it still needs enough identity consistency that friends recognize the person without reading the caption.

Write the intended use in plain language before choosing the package. "Three profile options for LinkedIn" leads to a different choice than "a private album of cinematic portraits for a birthday surprise." That short sentence helps you avoid buying a style because it looks exciting while missing the use case that actually matters.

Quick comparison

Package goalBest source-photo matchReview focus
Professional headshotsClear face detail, neutral clothing, low visual clutter.Identity, crop, expression, and background restraint.
Creator portraitsSeveral expressions, some outfit variety, natural body posture.Personality, usable crops, and social profile fit.
Themed albumsStable identity photos plus one clear mood direction.Scene consistency, costume fit, and artifact checks.
Small test setYour sharpest two or three current portraits.Whether the direction is worth a larger credit spend.

Use related guides as planning tools

Before starting, read source-photo guidance and private gallery notes. Then open packages and compare the package description, credit cost, and intended output. That creates a simple decision path: purpose first, source-photo fit second, credits third.

A simple package-choice framework

  • Need one polished identity look? Choose headshots or profile portraits.
  • Need expressive social content? Choose creator, lifestyle, beauty, or themed album sets.
  • Need a specific event mood? Choose holiday, sports, wedding, fan, or cinematic packages.
  • Need to test first? Start smaller, review privately, then spend more credits when the direction is clear.

Package planning FAQ

Should I start with the smallest package?

Start small when you are testing a new look, a new source-photo set, or a dramatic style. Choose a larger package when the intended use is clear and you already know the source photos represent you well.

How do I avoid wasting credits?

Check three things before generation: whether the package matches the final use, whether the source photos are clear enough, and whether the visible credit cost feels right for the number of images you expect to review.

Can one package cover every style?

Usually no. A focused package creates a cleaner gallery. If you want professional headshots and cinematic posters, treat them as separate requests so each set has a clear visual job.

The best package is not always the biggest one. It is the one that fits your source photos, your intended use, and the amount of review you want before downloading favorites.

settings.summary: Understand how MyDreamShoots customers review finished images, track credit use, compare outputs, and keep private albums organized after generation.
settings.author: MyDreamShoots editorial team
settings.imageAlt: MyDreamShoots private gallery workspace for reviewing generated images
settings.body:
Generation is only one part of the customer workflow. After a private job finishes, the gallery helps you compare images, download favorites, and understand how credits moved through the request.

Where finished images land

Finished MyDreamShoots images return to the signed-in account that started the job. Keeping outputs account-scoped makes it easier to review a set later, revisit downloads, and separate personal albums from public sharing choices.

How credit history stays readable

Credits are designed to be visible before generation begins. A request may reserve credits while it runs, settle them after successful delivery, or release them when a failed request cannot complete. Reviewing account history helps you connect a finished album to the package that created it.

That record is also useful when several people in the same household are comparing different looks. The gallery title, package choice, and credit movement give each set a simple paper trail, so a test run does not get confused with a polished request you meant to download later.

Review before sharing

Look at face consistency, hand detail, background artifacts, crop quality, and whether the scene matches the package promise. Some images may be better for profile use, while others work better as private keepsakes or social drafts.

For public-facing downloads, also test the image at the size where it will actually appear. A portrait that looks strong in the gallery may reveal edge artifacts once cropped into a small avatar, while a quieter frame can work better for a resume, booking profile, or team page because the face stays readable.

Organize downloads by purpose

Download favorites into folders that match their use: profile, professional, holiday, creator, event, or archive. This small habit helps you avoid mixing experimental images with polished images you plan to use publicly.

When to run another set

Start another request when the first gallery shows a clear direction to improve. If expressions are strong but lighting feels off, adjust package mood or source-photo notes. If identity is inconsistent, improve the source photo set before spending more credits.

Turn gallery review into feedback

A useful gallery review is specific. Instead of deciding that a set is simply good or bad, note what worked: the best lighting, the strongest expression, the most believable crop, and the package mood that felt closest to the goal. Then note what should change before another request. Maybe the next set needs clearer source photos, fewer dramatic costume cues, or a tighter brief around professional use.

This record does not need a formal spreadsheet. A few notes beside the downloaded favorites are enough. The point is to make the next credit spend more informed than the last one, especially when you are testing a new visual direction.

What to check before downloading favorites

Review pointWhat to look forWhat to do next
IdentityThe face should feel consistent across the best images.If it drifts, improve source-photo clarity before another run.
Hands and edgesCheck fingers, hair edges, glasses, jewelry, and clothing lines.Use cleaner crops publicly and keep experiments private.
Scene promiseThe image should match the package mood you selected.If the mood is close but not exact, refine the next brief.
Download useProfile crops need different checks than keepsake images.Save separate folders for profile, social, archive, and tests.

Private gallery checklist

  • Confirm the finished set belongs to the right account.
  • Review identity, crop, and background quality before downloading.
  • Check credit movement in account history.
  • Save public-use favorites separately from experiments.
  • Use what you learned before choosing the next package.

Private gallery FAQ

Are finished images public by default?

No. The article flow is built around account-scoped review. You decide which downloads are suitable for public profiles, social posts, or private keepsakes.

Why does credit history matter?

Credit history helps connect a finished album to the package and generation request that produced it. That is useful when comparing tests, planning a second pass, or reviewing billing questions.

What should I do with imperfect results?

Do not treat every output as a final image. Use imperfect frames as feedback: they can show whether the next request needs clearer source photos, a calmer package, or a more specific style note.

A private gallery is most useful when it becomes a review space, not just a download folder. Treat each set as feedback for the next one.

settings.title: Creator: how to plan this MyDreamShoots photo package category
settings.summary: Use this MyDreamShoots guide to decide when Creator fits, which source photos or references help, what to compare before spending credits, and how to review finished images privately.
settings.author: MyDreamShoots editorial team
settings.imageAlt: MyDreamShoots Creator package category cover
settings.body:
The Creator package category has a specific job inside MyDreamShoots: Creator portraits, profile cards, product-style scenes, social cards, and private personal-brand albums. It works best when the request has one clear use, a small set of dependable source photos, and a private review plan before anything is downloaded or shared.

When Creator is the right fit

Use Creator when the finished images need to support a personal brand, creator profile, campaign draft, or social-facing album. This is the category to choose when creator portraits, profile cards, product-style scenes, and social cards match the result you want from the next photo set. If the goal is still vague, start by naming the final use: profile update, creator album, keepsake, announcement, social draft, or a short motion test.

The strongest creator requests keep style and purpose in the same lane. A customer who needs a calm work portrait should not judge the same set by the standards of a dramatic scene package. A customer who wants a themed private album should allow more mood, but still check whether the person remains recognizable.

What to prepare before choosing it

Prepare clear face photos plus one or two frames that show posture, shoulders, and the kind of outfit tone you want the creator set to follow. Treat the source photos as identity evidence first. Style references, outfit notes, destination cues, fan details, or movement ideas should support the request after the person is already clear.

For a first pass, keep the input set smaller and cleaner than a social camera roll. Use current images, avoid heavy filters, and separate unrelated goals into different private jobs. MyDreamShoots can follow a focused brief more reliably than a folder that asks for several looks at once.

How to compare Creator with nearby choices

Compare creator against neighboring packages by the decision it helps you make, not only by which cover image looks strongest. The table below turns the category into a practical choice before credit cost is confirmed.

Decision pointUse Creator whenReview after generation
Final useUse Creator when the finished images need to support a personal brand, creator profile, campaign draft, or social-facing album.Review crop variety, face consistency, personal-brand tone, and whether the images can work as headers, avatars, or social posts.
source photosPrepare clear face photos plus one or two frames that show posture, shoulders, and the kind of outfit tone you want the creator set to follow.Check whether the clearest input details carried through the best images.
Category examplescreator portraits, profile cards, product-style scenes, and social cardsKeep the outputs that match the chosen example instead of mixing several directions.
Credit planUse a focused first pass when the style is new.Decide whether the next request should repeat, expand, or change direction.

Credit and private gallery planning

Before the job starts, review the visible credit cost and ask whether the category is carrying the right amount of work. If you only need to test creator, a smaller request can teach you what works. If the final use is already clear, a broader gallery may be easier to judge because it gives more crops and expressions to compare.

Finished outputs belong in the signed-in private gallery first. Use that space to compare identity, crop, expression, background detail, and whether the package category actually delivered the mood you selected. Download favorites only after separating public-use images from experiments.

Details to review before download

Review crop variety, face consistency, personal-brand tone, and whether the images can work as headers, avatars, or social posts. Also check small visual details that often decide whether a result is ready for a profile, card, post, or archive: face consistency, hand and hair edges, clothing lines, background distractions, and whether the image still reads well at the crop size where you will use it.

Creator images depend on recognizable personality cues: expression, gesture, color, and crop shape. This is where Creator becomes more than a menu label. The visible mood should explain why the category was chosen, while the private gallery keeps the customer in control of what stays personal and what becomes a downloaded favorite.

Mistakes to avoid

Avoid mixing product lifestyle shots with unrelated portrait goals unless the request is explicitly about creator-commerce imagery. The fastest way to weaken creator results is to overload the request with unrelated goals. Do not ask one job to be a professional portrait, a themed album, a restoration pass, and a motion concept at the same time. Keep the category honest, then run a second request when the next direction is different enough to need its own review.

A planning pass before you spend credits

  • Name the exact use for the finished images.
  • Choose the clearest source photos before adding style references.
  • Match the request to creator portraits, profile cards, product-style scenes, and social cards, not every nearby category.
  • Review credit cost before generation starts.
  • Use the private gallery to compare results before downloading favorites.

For broader browsing, open Photo Packages and compare Creator with the categories around it. The best choice is the one that makes the review criteria obvious before the first image is generated.

Creator FAQ

Creator questions usually come down to source quality, scope, credit planning, and whether the finished images match the intended use.

Is Creator good for a first request?

Yes, if the intended use is clear and the source photos are current, sharp, and permission-safe. If you are testing a dramatic change, start narrower so the first private gallery can show whether the direction deserves a larger credit spend.

How many source photos should I prepare?

Use enough images to show identity, angle, and expression without adding confusion. A small set of clear portraits usually beats a large group of old, filtered, or mixed-purpose images.

When should I choose another category instead?

Choose another category when the review criteria change. If Creator is being judged by a different use case, style world, or motion need, split the work into a separate private job so credits support a clearer outcome.

Creator works best when it is treated as a focused planning choice. Prepare the right inputs, review the cost, and let the private gallery show what should happen next.

If the goal is still vague, start by naming the final use: profile update, creator album, keepsake, announcement, social draft, or a short motion test.

The strongest christmas photos requests keep style and purpose in the same lane. A customer who needs a calm work portrait should not judge the same set by the standards of a dramatic scene package. A customer who wants a themed private album should allow more mood, but still check whether the person remains recognizable.

What to prepare before choosing it

Prepare clear source photos, then add one style cue that matches Christmas Photos: expression, outfit tone, background mood, crop need, or final use. Treat the source photos as identity evidence first. Style references, outfit notes, destination cues, fan details, or movement ideas should support the request after the person is already clear.

For a first pass, keep the input set smaller and cleaner than a social camera roll. Use current images, avoid heavy filters, and separate unrelated goals into different private jobs. MyDreamShoots can follow a focused brief more reliably than a folder that asks for several looks at once.

settings.body:
The Holiday package category has a specific job inside MyDreamShoots: Holiday travel portraits, seasonal profile images, scenic cards, and private festive albums. It works best when the request has one clear use, a small set of dependable source photos, and a private review plan before anything is downloaded or shared.

When Holiday is the right fit

Use Holiday when Seasonal is the right broad direction but the next private gallery needs a more specific mood, format, or use case. This is the category to choose when Holiday and Seasonal match the result you want from the next photo set. If the goal is still vague, start by naming the final use: profile update, creator album, keepsake, announcement, social draft, or a short motion test.

The strongest holiday requests keep style and purpose in the same lane. A customer who needs a calm work portrait should not judge the same set by the standards of a dramatic scene package. A customer who wants a themed private album should allow more mood, but still check whether the person remains recognizable.

What to prepare before choosing it

Prepare clear source photos, then add one style cue that matches Holiday: expression, outfit tone, background mood, crop need, or final use. Treat the source photos as identity evidence first. Style references, outfit notes, destination cues, fan details, or movement ideas should support the request after the person is already clear.

For a first pass, keep the input set smaller and cleaner than a social camera roll. Use current images, avoid heavy filters, and separate unrelated goals into different private jobs. MyDreamShoots can follow a focused brief more reliably than a folder that asks for several looks at once.

How to compare Holiday with nearby choices

Compare holiday against neighboring packages by the decision it helps you make, not only by which cover image looks strongest. The table below turns the category into a practical choice before credit cost is confirmed.

Before the job starts, review the visible credit cost and ask whether the category is carrying the right amount of work. If you only need to test holiday, a smaller request can teach you what works. Details to review before download

Review whether the finished images match Holiday instead of drifting back into a generic Seasonal result. Also check small visual details that often decide whether a result is ready for a profile, card, post, or archive: face consistency, hand and hair edges, clothing lines, background distractions, and whether the image still reads well at the crop size where you will use it.

Do not ask one job to be a professional portrait, a themed album, a restoration pass, and a motion concept at the same time. The strongest background changer requests keep style and purpose in the same lane. A customer who needs a calm work portrait should not judge the same set by the standards of a dramatic scene package. A customer who wants a themed private album should allow more mood, but still check whether the person remains recognizable.

The Portrait retouch tool category has a specific job inside MyDreamShoots: Input: a portrait you own or have permission to retouch. Output: a private cleaned portrait that preserves identity. Best for: skin, flyaway, and lighting cleanup before delivery. Cost: credits are shown before paid edits. It works best when the request has one clear use, a small set of dependable source photos, and a private review plan before anything is downloaded or shared.

When Portrait retouch is the right fit

Use Portrait retouch when the customer needs the AI Photo Edit workflow to solve one visible job before generation or download. This is the category to choose when Retouch, AI Photo Edit, Portrait retouch, and /tools/portrait-retouch match the result you want from the next photo set. If the goal is still vague, start by naming the final use: profile update, creator album, keepsake, announcement, social draft, or a short motion test.

The strongest portrait retouch requests keep style and purpose in the same lane. A customer who needs a calm work portrait should not judge the same set by the standards of a dramatic scene package. A customer who wants a themed private album should allow more mood, but still check whether the person remains recognizable.

What to prepare before choosing it

Prepare source photos or finished gallery images that match Portrait retouch, then keep the tool brief focused on one edit, portrait, or motion need. Treat the source photos as identity evidence first. Style references, outfit notes, destination cues, fan details, or movement ideas should support the request after the person is already clear.

For a first pass, keep the input set smaller and cleaner than a social camera roll. Use current images, avoid heavy filters, and separate unrelated goals into different private jobs. MyDreamShoots can follow a focused brief more reliably than a folder that asks for several looks at once.

settings.title: KIDS Act
settings.body:
1. Service audience

MyDreamShoots is not directed to children under 13 and is not designed for child account creation. Customers should use the service only if they can lawfully manage an account or have permission from a parent or legal guardian.

2. COPPA-aware handling

The Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) applies to certain online services directed to children under 13 or knowingly collecting personal information from children under 13. MyDreamShoots does not knowingly collect account information directly from children under 13. If we learn that child personal information was provided without required consent, we will review and delete or restrict it as appropriate.

3. Photos of minors

Customers must not upload photos of minors unless they are the parent, legal guardian, or otherwise have the legal right and consent to use those images for the requested AI workflow. Minor images should never be used for deceptive, exploitative, unlawful, or unsafe purposes.

4. Parent or guardian requests

A parent or legal guardian may contact us to ask about access, deletion, or restriction of child-related information. We may request verification before acting on a sensitive privacy request.

5. DPDPA requests

California and other U.S. state privacy requests are handled in our DPDPA notice, including access, deletion, correction, opt-out, and appeal requests where applicable.

6. Contact

Email support@mydreamshoots.com for children's privacy or COPPA-related questions.

settings.title: Aidreamcapes FAQ
settings.subtitle: Answers about source photos, travel package choice, credits, privacy, delivery, and refunds.
settings.journeyDescriptions: Add clear source photos.|Pick a travel direction.|Spend visible credits.|Review the private gallery.

settings.question: Which source photos work best for Aidreamcapes?
settings.answer: Use recent, clear portraits with natural expressions, varied angles, and minimal filters. Add outfit or destination references when the package needs a specific travel feeling.

settings.question: How should I choose a travel package?
settings.answer: Start with the final use: Route Portrait Albums for a broad scene atlas, Coastal Light Sets for sea light, Old Quarter Walks for city texture, Alpine Trail Frames for open-air depth, and Postcard Story Sets for share-ready crops.

settings.question: Are Aidreamcapes uploads and galleries private?
settings.answer: Yes. Source photos, generation jobs, albums, credit records, and downloads stay connected to the signed-in customer account.

settings.question: When are credits spent?
settings.answer: Credits are visible before a request starts. A job reserves the needed credits first, successful results consume them, and failed requests can release them.

settings.question: Where do finished portraits arrive?
settings.answer: Finished travel portraits return to the private account gallery so customers can compare crops, download favorites, and decide what to share.

settings.question: Can unused credits be reviewed?
settings.answer: Unused purchased credits can be reviewed under the refund policy. Credits spent on successful generation jobs are generally not refundable.

settings.question: What remains after a plan is canceled?
settings.answer: Customers can keep access to existing private albums according to the site's account rules, while new premium requests may require an active plan or available credits.

settings.question: Which source photos work best for Aidreamcapes?
settings.answer: Use recent, clear portraits with natural expressions, varied angles, and minimal filters. Add outfit or destination references when the package needs a specific travel feeling.

settings.question: How should I choose a travel package?
settings.answer: Start with the final use: Route Portrait Albums for a broad scene atlas, Coastal Light Sets for sea light, Old Quarter Walks for city texture, Alpine Trail Frames for open-air depth, and Postcard Story Sets for share-ready crops.

settings.question: Are Aidreamcapes uploads and galleries private?
settings.answer: Yes. Source photos, generation jobs, albums, credit records, and downloads stay connected to the signed-in customer account.

settings.question: When are credits spent?
settings.answer: Credits are visible before a request starts. A job reserves the needed credits first, successful results consume them, and failed requests can release them.

settings.question: Where do finished portraits arrive?
settings.answer: Finished travel portraits return to the private account gallery so customers can compare crops, download favorites, and decide what to share.

settings.question: Can unused credits be reviewed?
settings.answer: Unused purchased credits can be reviewed under the refund policy. Credits spent on successful generation jobs are generally not refundable.

settings.question: What remains after a plan is canceled?
settings.answer: Customers can keep access to existing private albums according to the site's account rules, while new premium requests may require an active plan or available credits.

settings.title: Privacy policy
settings.body:
1. Information we collect

Aidreamcapes collects the information needed to operate a private AI portrait workspace: account email, authentication state, source photos, reference notes, package selections, prompts, generation settings, credit ledger events, checkout status, support messages, generated outputs, downloads, and basic device or request metadata used for security and reliability.

2. How we use information

We use this information to create requested travel portraits, reserve and settle credits, deliver private galleries, keep account history accurate, provide support, prevent misuse, troubleshoot failed jobs, improve source-photo guidance, and show the right workspace pages after sign-in.

3. Source photos and generated images

Uploads and generated results stay tied to the current Aidreamcapes site and signed-in customer account. They are not sold as stock images, published in public galleries, or transferred to unrelated storefronts by default. Infrastructure and AI providers may process files only as needed to complete the service requested by the customer.

4. Payments, credits, and retention

Payments are handled by a connected payment provider. Aidreamcapes stores order IDs, checkout status, subscription state, credit purchases, reservations, reversals, and refund records; it does not store full card numbers on its own servers. Account records and generated assets are retained while needed for delivery, support, compliance, security, and customer access.

5. Customer choices and contact

Customers can contact support to ask about access, deletion, correction, privacy review, or account-specific delivery questions. Email support@aidreamcapes.com and include the account email plus any relevant order, job, or gallery details so the request can be reviewed safely.

settings.title: Refund policy
settings.body:
1. Refund eligibility

Refund requests are reviewed based on credit use, checkout status, subscription state, and whether generation work has already been completed. Unused one-time credit purchases may be eligible for review within the stated support window, while credits already consumed by successful travel generations are generally not refundable.

2. Failed or interrupted jobs

If a service-side technical failure prevents generation or private gallery delivery, Aidreamcapes may release reserved credits, rerun the request, provide troubleshooting, or review a refund. Support may ask for the account email, package name, job status, approximate request time, and any error message shown in the workspace.

3. Subscriptions and renewals

Canceling a subscription stops future renewals but does not automatically refund credits already granted or spent. Subscription refunds depend on payment status, usage, local requirements, and whether credits from the billing period have been applied to completed generations.

4. Non-refundable cases

Refunds are usually not available for dissatisfaction caused by unclear source photos, unsupported requests, changed creative preferences after generation, or outputs that were delivered according to the selected package. Customers should review source-photo guidance before starting a package run.

5. How to request review

Email support@aidreamcapes.com with the Aidreamcapes account email, checkout reference if available, package or job details, and a short explanation. Support will review the ledger and delivery records before deciding whether to release credits, rerun work, or refund eligible payments.

Upload only portraits, product references, wardrobe notes, location inspiration, or creative direction that you own, created, licensed, or have permission to use. Generated results should not be presented as factual documentary evidence of events that did not happen.

settings.title: How to plan source photos for cinematic AI travel portraits
settings.summary: Choose clear portraits, route-aware outfit notes, and focused references so Aidreamcapes can build cleaner private destination albums.
settings.author: Aidreamcapes editorial team
settings.imageAlt: Aidreamcapes route portrait album cover
settings.body:
Strong Aidreamcapes results begin before a destination scene is generated. The private workflow needs clear portraits first, then route mood, outfit notes, and atmosphere references that support the album direction without overloading it.

Start with identity clarity

Choose recent portraits where the face is sharp, naturally lit, and easy to recognize. Avoid heavy filters, sunglasses, harsh shadows, and group photos when the request needs consistent solo travel portraits.

For paired or family-style route albums, keep the same rule for every person in the set. One clear portrait for each subject is better than a folder where one person appears in crisp light and another is only visible in distant vacation photos.

Add destination context intentionally

A coastal set may need warm light, linen textures, and relaxed posture notes. An old quarter walk can use cafe, plaza, stone street, and boutique hotel references. A trail album benefits from outdoor layers, weather notes, and preferred season.

Helpful context can also include what should stay out of the scene. If the album should feel like a quiet hotel morning, say that instead of leaving room for nightlife, crowded streets, or heavy fashion styling. Boundaries keep the route believable and make the finished gallery easier to review.

Match wardrobe notes to the route

Wardrobe does not need to be complicated. Light neutrals can work for beach and resort scenes. Structured jackets can fit city routes. Outdoor layers support alpine or road-trip moods. Use wardrobe notes to make the destination believable, not to rewrite every detail of the person.

Keep the request focused

settings.title: How to choose destination mood references for AI travel portraits
settings.summary: A guide to choosing coastal, city, resort, trail, and postcard references that give Aidreamcapes a focused route mood without making the request noisy.
settings.author: Aidreamcapes editorial team
settings.imageAlt: Aidreamcapes route moodboard cover
settings.body:
Destination references work best when they behave like a compass. They should point Aidreamcapes toward light, texture, season, and route mood without asking one private job to become every trip at once.

Choose one primary mood

Start by naming the main feeling of the album: coastal calm, old city walk, island resort, mountain trail, rainy city break, market morning, or postcard journey. A precise mood helps every generated image feel like part of the same route.

The primary mood should be specific enough that you could reject a wrong image quickly. If the brief says "quiet harbor morning," a neon nightlife frame is clearly off-route. If the brief only says "travel vibe," almost anything can pass, which makes the final gallery harder to judge.

Use observable reference details

Useful references describe what the viewer can see: warm sea light, stone streets, shaded cafes, rooftop skyline, pine trail, linen outfit, soft rain, or golden hour. Avoid vague instructions that sound good but do not tell the scene what to show.

Good reference notes often combine one place texture, one light direction, and one wardrobe signal. For example, a shaded cafe lane, late-afternoon side light, and relaxed neutral layers give the album a practical direction without forcing every frame to copy the same background.

Limit the number of references

Two or three focused references are usually easier to follow than a large mixed board. If one reference is for lighting, one for route texture, and one for wardrobe tone, the package has a cleaner brief.

Separate conflicting routes

A desert road set and a rain-soaked city album can both be beautiful, but they should not fight inside the same generation request. Split them into separate private albums so credits support a clear outcome.

Turn references into a short brief

A strong brief can be one sentence: "Warm coastal portraits with relaxed linen styling, soft sunset light, and a private resort balcony mood." That gives the workflow a destination, visual texture, and wardrobe direction.

Reference quality check

Reference typeUseful detail
LightGolden hour, soft overcast, shaded cafe, bright coast.
Place textureStone streets, balcony, boardwalk, trail overlook, market lane.
Wardrobe toneNeutral layers, resort linen, structured city jacket, outdoor shell.
Album useProfile, keepsake, postcard crop, family route, creator story.

Bad references to leave out

Leave out references that conflict with the route. A snowy street, tropical beach, desert road, and luxury hotel lobby can all be attractive, but together they create a confused request. Also avoid references where the subject is hidden, the lighting is too stylized to read, or the main value is a celebrity pose rather than observable place details.

When a reference is mostly about mood, translate it into visible words. Instead of "make it cinematic," name the thing that creates the mood: dusk light, wet pavement, quiet balcony, market color, soft hotel window light, or a clean horizon.

Make references work together

Think of each reference as having a job. One image can define light, another can define place texture, and a third can suggest wardrobe tone. If two references are doing the same job, keep the clearer one. If a reference introduces a new season, city, color palette, or camera mood, ask whether it helps the route or simply adds noise.

A focused route board often feels quieter than a social media moodboard. That is a strength. Aidreamcapes can follow a small set of visible cues more easily than a collage of beautiful but conflicting travel ideas.

Destination reference FAQ

Can I use a moodboard?

Yes, but keep it small. Two or three references with different jobs are stronger than a large board where every image competes for attention.

Should references show people?

They can, but they do not have to. A place, color palette, lighting condition, or route texture can be more useful than another person's pose, especially when your own source portraits already carry identity.

How specific should the route brief be?

Specific enough to guide the album, but short enough to stay readable. One route, one lighting direction, one wardrobe tone, and one intended use are usually enough for a first request.

Good mood references make the final gallery feel planned. They give the route a visual language before the first image is generated.

settings.title: Route albums and credits: planning a private Aidreamcapes set
settings.summary: Plan a private Aidreamcapes route album by matching destination scope, output needs, review time, and visible credit cost before generation starts.
settings.author: Aidreamcapes editorial team
settings.imageAlt: Aidreamcapes shared route album cover
settings.body:
A route album is more than a single travel portrait. It is a small visual story, so the best credit plan starts with scope: how many scenes you need, how experimental the destination mood is, and how much review you want before sharing favorites.

Define the album scope

Decide whether you need one polished profile set, a wider route story, or a keepsake album with multiple crops. A focused city profile may need fewer outputs than a route album that covers arrival, walk, overlook, cafe, and postcard frames.

Scope also affects how you review the results. A profile refresh can be judged by one or two strong hero images. A route album needs continuity: similar light, believable wardrobe, and enough variety that the gallery feels like a short trip rather than repeated versions of the same frame.

Review credit cost before starting

Aidreamcapes shows credit cost before a private generation request begins. Use that step to decide whether the album should be a first test, a full route set, or a follow-up after improving source portraits and references.

Budget for iteration

Travel mood can be sensitive to lighting, wardrobe, and route details. If you are testing a new destination style, leave room for a second pass. The first gallery can teach you which source photos, outfit notes, or reference details to refine.

Keep private review in the plan

Finished images return to the account gallery, where you can compare consistency before downloading. Review time matters because some frames may become profile images, while others belong in a private keepsake album.

Avoid spending credits on mixed routes

The easiest way to waste a route album is to ask for several trips at once. A cafe morning, mountain overlook, marina walk, and rainy city night can all belong in the larger travel imagination, but they compete when one request needs a coherent gallery. Pick the route that best fits the source photos and save the other ideas for later.

This does not make the album less creative. It makes the review clearer. When the route is focused, you can judge whether identity, lighting, clothing, and scene texture improved together instead of trying to untangle too many changes at once.

Match album size to the use

Album useCredit planning approachPrivate review focus
Profile refreshChoose a tighter set with one route mood.Face consistency, crop, and clean background detail.
Route storyPlan for several scenes in the same destination language.Whether the album feels connected from image to image.
Gift or keepsakeLeave room for a second pass if the mood is personal.Expression, warmth, and whether the image feels believable.
Creator contentBudget for crop variety and a few stronger scene options.Which images can work as headers, posts, or thumbnails.

Choose the next route from what worked

If coastal light fits the subject well, build a second album around resort, island, or harbor scenes. If city texture works better, try old quarter, market morning, rooftop, or rainy street sets. Let the first private gallery guide the next credit spend.

Credit planning checklist

  • Name the route mood before choosing the package.
  • Match source-photo quality to the ambition of the album.
  • Check credit cost before generation starts.
  • Save room for a second pass when testing a new destination style.
  • Use the private gallery to decide what to download and what to improve.

Route credit FAQ

Should I run one large album first?

Run a larger album when the route direction is already clear. If you are testing a new destination mood, a focused first pass can show whether the source photos and references are working before you spend more credits.

What counts as a good first pass?

A good first pass does not need every image to be final. It should show stable identity, a believable route mood, and enough usable frames to decide whether the next request should expand, repeat, or change direction.

How should I compare two route ideas?

Compare one variable at a time. If both source photos and route mood change between requests, it becomes harder to know what improved the gallery.

Credits are easiest to manage when each request has a clear purpose. Plan the route, review the cost, then let the private gallery show you what the next album should become.

The Route Portraits package category has a specific job inside Aidreamcapes: Location-led AI portrait packages for coasts, resorts, old cities, and scenic overlooks. It works best when the request has one clear use, a small set of dependable source portraits, and a private review plan before anything is downloaded or shared.

When Route Portraits is the right fit

Use Route Portraits when the destination itself should guide the album through coast, city, resort, or lookout scenes. This is the category to choose when coastal light sets, old city walks, resort balcony scenes, and scenic outlooks match the result you want from the next route album. If the goal is still vague, start by naming the final use: profile update, creator album, keepsake, announcement, social draft, or a short motion test.

The strongest route portraits requests keep style and purpose in the same lane. A customer who needs a calm work portrait should not judge the same set by the standards of a dramatic scene package. A customer who wants a themed private album should allow more mood, but still check whether the person remains recognizable.

What to prepare before choosing it

Prepare clear portraits plus one route mood, one lighting direction, and simple outfit notes that fit the destination. Treat the source portraits as identity evidence first. Style references, outfit notes, destination cues, fan details, or movement ideas should support the request after the person is already clear.

For a first pass, keep the input set smaller and cleaner than a social camera roll. Use current images, avoid heavy filters, and separate unrelated goals into different private jobs. Aidreamcapes can follow a focused brief more reliably than a folder that asks for several looks at once.

Credit and private gallery planning

Before the job starts, review the visible credit cost and ask whether the category is carrying the right amount of work. If you only need to test route portraits, a smaller request can teach you what works. If the final use is already clear, a broader gallery may be easier to judge because it gives more crops and expressions to compare.

Finished outputs belong in the signed-in private gallery first. Use that space to compare identity, crop, expression, background detail, and whether the package category actually delivered the mood you selected. Download favorites only after separating public-use images from experiments.

Details to review before download

Review whether the person stays recognizable while the place texture, light, and route continuity feel believable. Also check small visual details that often decide whether a result is ready for a profile, card, post, or archive: face consistency, hand and hair edges, clothing lines, background distractions, and whether the image still reads well at the crop size where you will use it.

Route portraits use place texture, horizon lines, street scale, balcony light, and travel posture to tell the album story. This is where Route Portraits becomes more than a menu label. The visible mood should explain why the category was chosen, while the private gallery keeps the customer in control of what stays personal and what becomes a downloaded favorite.

Mistakes to avoid

Avoid asking one route request to cover several destinations that do not share light, wardrobe, or season. The fastest way to weaken route portraits results is to overload the request with unrelated goals. Do not ask one job to be a professional portrait, a themed album, a restoration pass, and a motion concept at the same time. Keep the category honest, then run a second request when the next direction is different enough to need its own review.

Is Route Portraits good for a first request?

How many source portraits should I prepare?

Use enough images to show identity, angle, and expression without adding confusion. A small set of clear portraits usually beats a large group of old, filtered, or mixed-purpose images.

settings.question: Can unused credits be reviewed?
settings.answer: Unused purchased credits can be reviewed under the refund policy. Credits spent on successful generation jobs are generally not refundable.

settings.question: What remains after a plan is canceled?

settings.title: KIDS Act
settings.body:
1. Service audience

Aidreamcapes is not directed to children under 13 and is not designed for child account creation. Customers should use the service only if they can lawfully manage an account or have permission from a parent or legal guardian.

2. COPPA-aware handling

The Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) applies to certain online services directed to children under 13 or knowingly collecting personal information from children under 13. Aidreamcapes does not knowingly collect account information directly from children under 13. If we learn that child personal information was provided without required consent, we will review and delete or restrict it as appropriate.

3. Photos of minors

Customers must not upload photos of minors unless they are the parent, legal guardian, or otherwise have the legal right and consent to use those images for the requested AI workflow. Minor images should never be used for deceptive, exploitative, unlawful, or unsafe purposes.

4. Parent or guardian requests

A parent or legal guardian may contact us to ask about access, deletion, or restriction of child-related information. We may request verification before acting on a sensitive privacy request.

5. CISA requests

California and other U.S. state privacy requests are handled in our CISA notice, including access, deletion, correction, opt-out, and appeal requests where applicable.

6. Contact

Email support@aidreamcapes.com for children's privacy or COPPA-related questions.

settings.body:
1. Subidas permitidas

Sube fotos propias o autorizadas, con personas identificables solo cuando tienes permiso para usarlas.

2. Contenido no permitido

No solicites suplantacion, acoso, abuso, desnudez no consentida, menores en contextos sensibles, documentos privados o usos ilegales.

3. Paquetes creativos

Los estilos de AIdreamshoots deben usarse para retratos, perfiles, pareja, creador, belleza o albumes privados dentro de un uso responsable.

4. Revision

Podemos bloquear pedidos, rechazar instrucciones o retirar resultados que infrinjan esta politica.

5. Contacto

Escribe a support@aidreamshoots.eu para dudas de contenido.

settings.subtitle: Como cuidamos cuentas, selfies fuente, creditos, pedidos y albumes privados.

settings.body:
1. Informacion que tratamos

AIdreamshoots usa el correo de cuenta, sesiones, selfies fuente, selecciones de paquete, instrucciones creativas, resultados generados, pedidos, suscripciones, movimientos de creditos, mensajes de soporte y senales tecnicas necesarias para seguridad y fiabilidad.

2. Uso de la informacion

Usamos esos datos para crear retratos solicitados, reservar y liquidar creditos, entregar albumes privados, resolver incidencias, prevenir abuso, mejorar guias de fotos fuente y mostrar el espacio privado correcto despues de iniciar sesion.

3. Fotos privadas

Las subidas y resultados quedan ligados a la cuenta del cliente en aidreamshoots.eu. No se venden como imagenes de stock ni se publican en galerias abiertas por defecto.

4. Pagos y conservacion

Los pagos se procesan con un proveedor conectado. Guardamos referencias de pedido, pago, reservas, devoluciones y suscripcion, no numeros completos de tarjeta. Algunos registros se conservan para soporte, seguridad, cumplimiento y acceso del cliente.

5. Opciones del cliente

Puedes pedir acceso, correccion, eliminacion o revision escribiendo a support@aidreamshoots.eu con el correo de la cuenta y el pedido afectado.

Al usar AIdreamshoots, crear cuenta, comprar creditos, subir fotos o iniciar un paquete aceptas estos terminos.

2. Uso permitido

Debes subir imagenes propias o con permiso, usar instrucciones licitas y evitar contenido que vulnere privacidad, identidad, propiedad intelectual o normas de seguridad.

3. Creditos y pedidos

Los creditos se muestran antes de generar. Pueden reservarse, gastarse, liberarse o devolverse segun el estado del pedido y la politica aplicable.

4. Resultados

Los albumes se entregan digitalmente en la cuenta privada. La calidad depende de fotos fuente, paquete, disponibilidad tecnica y reglas de proveedor.

5. Soporte

Para cuenta, pedidos o terminos, escribe a support@aidreamshoots.eu.

seo.title: Politica de contenido | AIdreamcapes
seo.description: Politica creativa de AIdreamcapes para fotos fuente, escenas de destino, seguridad y limites de publicacion.
seo.keywords: AIdreamcapes,politica de contenido,retratos de viaje,creditos de ruta,galeria privada

settings.body:
1. Subidas permitidas

Sube retratos, referencias de vestuario, inspiracion de lugar o notas creativas sobre las que tengas derechos o permiso.

2. Contenido no permitido

No uses AIdreamcapes para suplantacion, acoso, abuso, desnudez no consentida, menores en contextos sensibles, documentos privados o fines ilegales.

3. Escenas de destino

Las rutas visuales deben describir ambientes, luz y narrativa sin reclamar ubicaciones reales falsas o permisos que no existen.

4. Revision

Podemos rechazar pedidos o retirar salidas que violen esta politica.

5. Contacto

Escribe a support@aidreamcapes.eu para revisar una solicitud.

seo.title: Politica de cookies | AIdreamcapes
seo.description: AIdreamcapes usa cookies necesarias para acceso, creditos, rutas guardadas, soporte y entrega de galerias.
seo.keywords: AIdreamcapes,politica de cookies,retratos de viaje,creditos de ruta,galeria privada

settings.body:
1. Continuidad de ruta

AIdreamcapes usa cookies necesarias y almacenamiento local para reconocer la sesion, conservar elecciones de destino, proteger formularios y mantener pagos o galerias de viaje en curso.

2. Diagnostico operativo

Usamos senales tecnicas acotadas para revisar rendimiento, intentos de abuso, errores de ruta, estado de credito y disponibilidad de entrega.

3. Preferencias del cliente

La gestion se realiza desde el navegador. Al desactivar cookies esenciales, algunas rutas, pagos, accesos o galerias privadas pueden dejar de funcionar.

4. Contacto

Para consultas sobre cookies de AIdreamcapes escribe a support@aidreamcapes.eu.

seo.title: Politica de privacidad | AIdreamcapes
seo.description: AIdreamcapes resume privacidad para retratos fuente, rutas visuales, pagos, galerias y soporte de cuenta.
seo.keywords: AIdreamcapes,politica de privacidad,retratos de viaje,creditos de ruta,galeria privada

settings.body:
1. Informacion que tratamos

AIdreamcapes usa correo de cuenta, sesiones, fotos fuente, notas de ruta, paquete elegido, instrucciones creativas, resultados, pedidos, movimientos de creditos, mensajes de soporte y metadatos tecnicos para operar una galeria privada de viaje.

2. Uso de la informacion

Usamos esos datos para crear retratos de destino, mantener saldo y pedidos correctos, entregar galerias privadas, solucionar fallos, prevenir abuso y mejorar la orientacion de escena.

3. Fotos y rutas privadas

Las subidas y resultados permanecen asociados al sitio aidreamcapes.eu y a la cuenta iniciada. No se transfieren a otros escaparates ni se publican como muestras publicas por defecto.

4. Pagos y conservacion

Los pagos los procesa un proveedor conectado. Conservamos estados de pago, ordenes, suscripciones, reservas, reversiones y reembolsos cuando es necesario para soporte, cumplimiento y seguridad.

5. Opciones del cliente

Para acceso, eliminacion, correccion o privacidad, escribe a support@aidreamcapes.eu e incluye email de cuenta y datos del pedido.

seo.title: Politica de reembolsos | AIdreamcapes
seo.description: Consulta el proceso de AIdreamcapes para revisar creditos de ruta, entregas incompletas y reembolsos de viaje.
seo.keywords: AIdreamcapes,politica de reembolsos,retratos de viaje,creditos de ruta,galeria privada

settings.body:
1. Elegibilidad

Las solicitudes se revisan segun uso de creditos, estado de pago, suscripcion y entrega de la galeria.

2. Creditos reservados

Si una ruta falla por un problema tecnico, soporte puede liberar la reserva, repetir el trabajo o emitir creditos de reemplazo.

3. Creditos usados

Los creditos de galerias entregadas normalmente no se reembolsan porque el procesamiento de escena ya fue consumido.

4. Calidad de fotos fuente

Fotos borrosas, baja luz, permisos insuficientes o notas contradictorias pueden limitar la elegibilidad.

5. Contacto

Escribe a support@aidreamcapes.eu con email de cuenta, pedido y ruta afectada.
